title: Intertherm Furnace Code 1 Blink: Ignition or flame-proving failure
meaning: The furnace entered system lockout after exceeding its ignition retries.
commonCauses: No gas reaching the burners
A failed hot-surface igniter
A dirty or weak flame sensor
diySteps: Confirm the thermostat is calling for heat and the gas shutoff has not been moved.
Turn furnace power off for five minutes, restore it once, and note whether the same code returns.
whenToCallPro: Call a licensed technician if ignition fails again after one reset or if you smell gas.
snippetAnswer: Intertherm furnace code 1 Blink means the furnace entered system lockout after exceeding its ignition retries on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Nortek single-stage condensing furnaces using the documented Emerson integrated control.

title: Intertherm Furnace Code 2 Blinks: Pressure switch was closed at the wrong time
meaning: The pressure switch was stuck closed when it should have been open.
commonCauses: A pressure switch stuck closed
A pinched or incorrectly connected pressure hose
Shorted pressure-switch wiring or a control fault
diySteps: Turn furnace power off for five minutes and do not bypass or jumper the pressure switch.
Check only the outdoor vent openings for obvious snow, ice, leaves, or nests before restoring power once.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if the code returns; the switch, hose, wiring, and inducer draft need testing.
snippetAnswer: Intertherm furnace code 2 Blinks means the pressure switch was stuck closed when it should have been open on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Nortek single-stage condensing furnaces using the documented Emerson integrated control.

title: Intertherm Furnace Code 3 Blinks: Pressure-switch circuit did not close
meaning: The pressure switch was stuck open when it should have closed.
commonCauses: A blocked intake or exhaust vent
A restricted condensate drain or pressure hose
A weak inducer motor or pressure switch
diySteps: With the furnace off, check outdoor intake and exhaust openings for snow, ice, leaves, or nests.
Replace a visibly dirty air filter, restore power once, and note whether the code returns.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if the vent is clear and the pressure-switch code returns; combustion-air testing requires instruments.
snippetAnswer: Intertherm furnace code 3 Blinks means the pressure switch was stuck open when it should have closed on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Nortek single-stage condensing furnaces using the documented Emerson integrated control.

title: Intertherm Furnace Code 4 Blinks: Limit circuit opened
meaning: The high-temperature limit switch is open.
commonCauses: A dirty or overly restrictive air filter
Closed or blocked supply and return vents
A blower, limit switch, or airflow problem
diySteps: Turn the furnace off and replace a dirty filter with the size and type specified for the system.
Open all supply registers and make sure return grilles are not blocked before trying one reset.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if the limit code returns; repeated overheating can damage the furnace.
snippetAnswer: Intertherm furnace code 4 Blinks means the high-temperature limit switch is open on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Nortek single-stage condensing furnaces using the documented Emerson integrated control.

title: Intertherm Furnace Code 5 Blinks: Flame detected when the gas valve should be off
meaning: Flame was sensed for more than four seconds while the gas valve was off.
commonCauses: A gas valve leaking or stuck open
A shorted flame-sensing circuit
A failed integrated control board
whenToCallPro: Turn the furnace off and call a licensed technician immediately to test the gas valve and flame-proving circuit.
dangerNote: Turn the furnace off and do not reset it. If you smell gas, leave the building without operating switches and contact the gas utility or emergency services from outside.
snippetAnswer: Intertherm furnace code 5 Blinks means flame was sensed for more than four seconds while the gas valve was off on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Nortek single-stage condensing furnaces using the documented Emerson integrated control.

title: Intertherm Furnace Code 6 Blinks: Flame-rollout safety lockout
commonCauses: A blocked flue or combustion-air path
A burner or gas-pressure problem
A damaged or restricted heat exchanger
whenToCallPro: Leave the furnace off and call a licensed technician for a combustion-safety inspection.
dangerNote: Keep the furnace off. Do not reset a rollout switch. If you smell gas or a carbon-monoxide alarm sounds, leave the building and contact emergency services or the gas utility.
snippetAnswer: Intertherm furnace code 6 Blinks means the flame-rollout switch is open on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Nortek single-stage condensing furnaces using the documented Emerson integrated control.

title: Intertherm Furnace Code 7 Blinks: Low flame-sensor signal
meaning: The control detected a low flame-sensor signal.
commonCauses: A dirty flame sensor
Poor furnace grounding or reversed polarity
Low gas pressure or an unstable burner flame
diySteps: Turn furnace power off and confirm its access panel is fully seated.
Try one reset and note whether the burners light briefly before shutting off.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if flame drops out again; flame current and combustion should be measured.
snippetAnswer: Intertherm furnace code 7 Blinks means the control detected a low flame-sensor signal on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Nortek single-stage condensing furnaces using the documented Emerson integrated control.

title: Intertherm Furnace Code 8 Blinks: Igniter circuit fault
meaning: The igniter relay reported a fault.
commonCauses: A cracked or open hot-surface igniter
Loose or damaged igniter wiring
A failed igniter relay on the control board
diySteps: Turn power off and look through the burner-viewing area for an obviously cracked igniter without touching it.
Restore power once and observe whether the igniter glows; do not continue resetting the furnace.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if the igniter does not glow or the fault returns.
snippetAnswer: Intertherm furnace code 8 Blinks means the igniter relay reported a fault on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Nortek single-stage condensing furnaces using the documented Emerson integrated control.
